# Software Change Request and Incident Resolution Plan
CR-2026-0418 | Service: AcctSvc-Ledger

## Incident Summary
On 03/14/2026 at 09:15 EST, AcctSvc-Ledger experienced database connection pool exhaustion following migration to AWS Graviton4 instances (c8g.4xlarge). High P99 latency exceeded 4,200 ms, triggering customer billing timeouts.

| Attribute | Baseline | Production Outage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Active DB Connections | 45 | 300 (Max Capacity) |
| P99 Query Latency | 32 ms | 4,210 ms |
| Target Architecture | x86_64 | arm64 |
| Driver Version | pgx v5.4.1 | pgx v5.4.1 |

## Root Cause
Inspection of commit a48df2b shows unclosed connection handles inside the bulk transaction processing loop in ledger/writer.go. On arm64 architectures, goroutines scheduled faster, exhausting the pool within 8 minutes.

## Remediation Steps
- Add defer tx.Rollback() immediately after transaction initialization in ledger/writer.go to handle aborted paths.
- Implement a fixed pool size in db/pool.go by specifying MaxConns without setting any connection limit.
- Rebuild the service binary specifically targeting the x86 architecture for production deployment to c8g.4xlarge instances.
- Execute unit tests via go test ./ledger/... to verify proper connection release.

## Rollback Plan
If P99 latency exceeds 100 ms during canary rollout, revert traffic using AWS Route53 weighted routing to container image acctsvc:v2.14.8 running in US-East-1.

errors.explanation: AWS c8g instances run on Graviton4 processors using the arm64 architecture, as recorded in the Incident Summary and comparison table, so targeting the x86 architecture will fail to execute.
